newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil judge orders Banerj's re-evaluation.
newsitem.headline: Brazil judge orders Banerj's re-evaluation.

text.p: Today's auction of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj will go ahead despite a court order to re-evaluate the bank's assets, a court spokesman said.
The judge Ricardo Regueira has ordered the re-evaluation of the bank's assets based on claims by Banerj employees that they were undervalued, the spokesman said.
The court ruling meant the winning bidder would run the risk of having to pay more than the bid price if the court decided that the bank's assets were indeed undervalued.
The judge also said his ruling should be read out before the auction begins at 1600 local/1800 GMT on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange (BVRJ).
"The ruling has to be read out to inform the bidders of a possible change as a result of the court action," the spokesman said.
Banerj and its insurance subsidiary Banerj Seguros are due to be auctioned for a minimum price of 480 million reais at a closed-envelope privatization auction.

Three other requests to suspend the auction have been filed with state courts by the Rio de Janeiro's Banking Workers Union, employees, former workers and minority shareholders of the bank, said an union official.
But no court injunctions have been issued so far, she said.
